text.arabic_uthmani: فَمَا وَجَدْنَا فِيهَا غَيْرَ بَيْتٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلْمُسْلِمِينَ

words.gloss_range: sequential or consequential connector launching the negated report from the preceding narrative
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) makes the ayah arrive as the next consequence of the preceding mission sequence, so the negative finding is not a detached audit. Its attachment to the following negator makes relation and denial land together before the verb appears, while the repeated boundary connector keeps extraction and finding inside one chain of results.

topics.headline: consequential narrative link
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah opens as a result in the mission sequence, not as a fresh disconnected negative statement.
topics.reason: The particle is tagged as a conjunction linking to the preceding mission, and the CRITICAL rows consistently read it as sequential, causal, and boundary-linking rather than independent content.

topics.headline: relation and negation fused at launch
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the connector and negator as a compressed opening unit, delaying the search verb until the relation and denial have already landed.
topics.reason: The surface proclitic directly precedes the negator, so the sound-shape and written launch support a compact fa-ma onset without adding a new lexical sense.

words.gloss_range: negative particle governing the perfect search verb and opening the restriction frame
words.prose: {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) first gives the report a completed negative field: the search has yielded absence, not a still-pending failure. That denial then waits for the later exception word, so the ayah moves from total non-finding to one counted survivor inside a single restriction frame.

topics.headline: completed negative search result
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the denial is a completed verdict over the search, not an unfinished or interrogative search question.
topics.reason: QAC identifies the word as the negative particle governing the perfect verb, and the attachment support warns that the negation must preserve restriction rather than loose contrast.

topics.headline: restriction opened before exception
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels suspense between the initial absence and the later single exception, so the survivor appears as the only breach in an otherwise empty result set.
topics.reason: The local construction pairs the negative particle with the later exception noun; the intervening verb and locative phrase sit inside that bracket.

words.gloss_range: completed first-person plural finding/search report under negation, with an explicit exception-object frame
words.root_gloss_range: finding, discovering, obtaining, assessing, and presence-related branches; local grammar selects completed search/find while allowing verdict pressure
words.prose: {{ar:وَجَدْنَا}} ({{tr:wajadnā}}) is the evidentiary core of the clause: a completed plural witness report under negation, not an ongoing search. The root {{ar:و ج د}} ({{tr:w-j-d}}) keeps locating primary, while the verdict context lets assessment and visible presence press on the line; the local Form I reports discovery of an existing remnant, not production of one. Positioned between denial, town-domain, and exception, the verb turns the preceding extraction scene (51:35) into an auditable search result.

topics.headline: completed plural witness verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a final witnessed audit: the speakers report what the completed search established under negation.
topics.reason: The verb is PV.1CP under the negative particle, and the local frame has explicit object and locative complements, supporting a completed plural report.

topics.headline: transitive verb makes exception the yield
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the paradox that what is grammatically found is the exception phrase, so absence and one surviving object are processed through the same verb.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the later exception noun the accusative object of this transitive verb, with the locative phrase intervening before the object appears.

topics.headline: finding remains primary with verdict pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the search is also an evaluation of the town's visible righteous presence, while locating remains the selected local sense.
topics.reason: The root family supports finding, judging, experiencing, and existence-related pressure, but the local object-plus-locative frame keeps actual search/finding primary.

topics.headline: discovery rather than causation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the witnesses discover an already existing remnant rather than bringing that remnant into being.
topics.reason: The local surface is Form I perfect, so causative creation or production language from related forms must stay outside the selected sense.

topics.headline: extraction answered by audit
topics.reader_payoff: The reader connects the prior extraction action (51:35) to this investigative verdict, so the ayah measures what the rescue scene left behind.
topics.reason: Rows explicitly connect the current plural finding report with the prior extraction scene (51:35), while QAC confirms the same first-person plural verb morphology.

words.gloss_range: preposition plus feminine pronoun marking the bounded town-domain searched under negation
words.prose: {{ar:فِيهَا}} ({{tr:fīhā}}) turns the non-finding into absence inside a specific town-domain, not a global statement. The fused preposition and feminine suffix keep the implied settlement present without renaming it, and the word's position before the exception lets the listener first feel the wide searched space and then the contraction to one house. Its recurrence around the boundary links extraction (51:35), search (51:36), and sign-space (51:37).

topics.headline: bounded interior search-space
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the absence is measured inside a defined town-space before the single exception appears.
topics.reason: The locative phrase is syntactically attached to the search verb, and translation support identifies the feminine suffix as the settlement domain carried from context.

topics.headline: feminine suffix carries the settlement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader keeps the implied town in view through the pronoun rather than needing the town to be renamed.
topics.reason: Attachment cross-reference evidence treats the suffix as a discourse-inferred reference to the same destroyed settlement, while QAC identifies the form as preposition plus 3fs suffix.

topics.headline: physical and social containment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the search-space is both geographic and social: the issue is a moral population inside a place, not empty geography.
topics.reason: The locative syntax establishes physical interiority, while the following classification of people makes the searched domain socially charged.

topics.headline: locative chain across adjacent ayahs
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks the same place shifting roles from rescue domain (51:35), to absence-domain (51:36), to sign-domain (51:37).
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give concrete adjacent references, and the attachment evidence supports continuity of the feminine locative referent.

words.gloss_range: accusative exception noun functioning as the found object and governing the following house noun
words.root_gloss_range: otherness, difference, alteration, and related jealousy/protective branches; local grammar selects exception/other-than while retaining outlier pressure
words.prose: {{ar:غَيْرَ}} ({{tr:ghayra}}) is where the negative report turns: the exception itself occupies the object position and governs the following house noun, so the found thing is grammatically an outlier from everything else not found. The root {{ar:غ ي ر}} ({{tr:gh-y-r}}) gives difference and alteration pressure, but the local noun form selects exception rather than narrating a change. As the middle pivot, it closes the not-except restriction and moves the ayah from absence to the single classified remnant.

topics.headline: exception phrase as found object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the exception is not an afterthought; it is the grammatical object through which the sole find appears.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the word the accusative direct object of the search verb and the idafa head governing the following house noun.

topics.headline: otherness colors the exception
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the house as the differing outlier inside a uniform negative result, while change and jealousy branches remain background color rather than local senses.
topics.reason: V4 includes otherness, alteration, and jealousy branches, but the local accusative exception noun selects other-than/except and blocks a verbal change reading.

topics.headline: negation turns to remnant
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the structural turn from total absence to the only surviving unit, with the restriction excluding every alternative find.
topics.reason: The negator and this exception noun form the local restriction frame, and the word begins the middle beat that redirects the report toward the house.

topics.headline: exception links to house and identity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the exception is not merely quantitative; it pairs with house-language and the final identity class to explain why this remnant differs.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows preserve a recognizable exception-house and exception-identity relation, while local syntax keeps the pairing inside the object phrase.

words.gloss_range: one indefinite house or household, genitive inside the exception phrase and completed by the following identity phrase
words.root_gloss_range: dwelling, lodging, household, shelter, night-stay, and extended container branches; local noun selects physical-social house while allowing shelter and endurance imagery
words.prose: {{ar:بَيْتٍۢ}} ({{tr:baytin}}) supplies the concrete content of the exception while remaining genitive inside that exception phrase. Its singular indefiniteness makes the remnant one unnamed count-unit, not a named household, and the root {{ar:ب ي ت}} ({{tr:b-y-t}}) lets that unit be both dwelling and household: a shelter-container whose identity is completed only by the final class phrase. Broader night, sacred-house, and household contrasts are real pressures, but locally they serve the image of one surviving domestic container inside the searched town, especially after the extraction scene (51:35) and against household scenes such as 51:26.

topics.headline: one unnamed house
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices scarcity as grammar: the remnant is one indefinite unit rather than a named or plural group.
topics.reason: QAC and noun-instance evidence identify the word as genitive, indefinite, masculine singular, and the rows use that form to preserve anonymity and minimal count.

topics.headline: house embedded in exception
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the house is the content of the exception, not an independent new subject detached from the restriction.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes this word the genitive complement of the exception noun, while the restriction frame makes it the concrete object-content.

topics.headline: dwelling and household together
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the counted structure also stands for the people it shelters, making the remnant a moral household-container.
topics.reason: Dictionary evidence supports dwelling and household senses, and the following class phrase requires the physical unit to carry social identity.

topics.headline: night and sacred-house pressures narrowed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can feel shelter, endurance, and sacred-house resonance without replacing the local sense of an ordinary surviving house.
topics.reason: The b-y-t family contains night-stay, sacred-house, and extended container branches, but the local concrete noun and indefinite syntax select house/household.

topics.headline: middle beat awaiting identity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the ayah count the remnant first and then wait for identity to explain why the one house matters.
topics.reason: The word sits between the exception noun and the prepositional class phrase; boundary rows tie it to the extracted group of 51:35 and to the narrowing from town-domain to household.

words.gloss_range: preposition governing the final identity phrase with partitive and characterizing readings both locally live
words.prose: {{ar:مِنَ}} ({{tr:mina}}) is the hinge between the counted house and the final identity class. Because the preposition remains independent, it can mark both membership from among submitters and characterization as a submitter-house; reducing it to only one side would lose either class-belonging or defining quality. It also keeps the classification inside the same compressed phrase rather than opening a new clause, and its nasal sound carries the ear from the single house into the class noun it governs.

topics.headline: two live classification readings
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the house is both from the submitter class and characterized by that class, so quantity and identity remain joined.
topics.reason: QAC marks the preposition as partitive or characterizing, and attachment evidence shows it governs the final class phrase as the house's characterization.

topics.headline: house linked directly to identity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the search result and identity label fused in one phrase, not separated into a later explanatory sentence.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the final plural and attaches it to the house phrase, making the final beat explanatory rather than a new object.

topics.headline: audible bridge into the class noun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears continuity from the single house into the final class term through the preposition's nasal sound.
topics.reason: The particle sits between the house and identity noun, so the phonetic observation is locally anchored to the same syntactic hinge.

words.gloss_range: definite masculine plural active participial class of submitters, governed by the preceding preposition as the house's classifier
words.root_gloss_range: submission, self-surrender, safety, soundness, peace, greeting, handover, and unrelated homonymous branches; local Form IV participial noun selects active submitter identity with peace/soundness coloring
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْمُسْلِمِينَ}} ({{tr:al-muslimīna}}) closes the ayah on identity rather than on the count of one house. As a definite active participial plural from {{ar:س ل م}} ({{tr:s-l-m}}), it presents recognizable people actively characterized by submission, while the root's peace and soundness pressures color the surviving household as an intact submitting unit. The final word also reframes the same remnant named with belief-language in 51:35 as submitters here, with 49:14 keeping the belief-submission distinction live but not forcing one category to erase the other. Its same-surah peace thread reaches back to 51:25, and its long final cadence lets the plural identity class carry the ayah's audible close.

topics.headline: active definite submitter class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final label is an active, definite class of submitters rather than an abstract quality or completed past event.
topics.reason: QAC tags the word as a genitive definite masculine plural active participle, and the CRITICAL rows align that form with ongoing agentive submission.

topics.headline: peace and surrender coloring without form shift
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can feel safety, soundness, peace, and handing-over pressure around the submitter label, while the actual form remains Form IV active submission rather than total capitulation or an unrelated branch.
topics.reason: The root family contains peace, safety, handover, and Form X surrender material, but the local surface is the Form IV active participial identity term.

topics.headline: identity seals the house exception
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees submission as the feature that explains why the one house is the exception and why the ayah lands on identity.
topics.reason: The preceding preposition governs this word as classifier for the house, and final position makes the identity class the audible and structural closure.

topics.headline: belief-language hands off to submission-language
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the adjacent shift from believers in 51:35 to submitters in 51:36, with 49:14 making that lexical distinction worth preserving.
topics.reason: Multiple CRITICAL rows give concrete references to 51:35 and 49:14, so the boundary shift is preserved without collapsing belief and submission into interchangeable labels.

topics.headline: local sound thread and final cadence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the final identity term as part of a same-surah peace/submission thread (51:25) and as the ayah's sustained closing cadence.
topics.reason: Rows explicitly connect the same root to earlier same-surah peace language (51:25) and to the nasal and long-vowel cadence of the final phrase.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **One shelter embodies yielded soundness.** `و ج د/B001` supplies finding; `غ ي ر/B005` exception; `ب ي ت/B001` shelter/dwelling; `س ل م/B001` soundness and safety. The restrictive grammar isolates one house from the settlement. I infer **household soundness -> identifiable refuge-unit -> extraction**. The house is social and ethical shelter, not only architecture.
2. **Submission is handing over rather than resistance.** `س ل م/B012` supplies handing over/consigning an affair, activated against the resistant peoples of 51:39, 44, 46. I infer **consigned allegiance -> no oppositional struggle against the warning**. This remains distinct from the safety branch and is anchored in *muslimīn*.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 51:55's focus on believers made the isolated house newly legible as a receptive social unit, not simply the last standing building.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **A household is the minimum surviving unit of safe surrender.** **Lexical evidence:** fixed `و ج د/B001` is finding or coming upon, with `B002` existence found in reality; fixed `غ ي ر/B005` is exception and negation; fixed `ب ي ت/B002` is “household and family”; fixed `س ل م/B001` is soundness and safety, while `B012` selects handing over and letting go. **Structural cue:** extraction precedes at 51:35; a residual sign, Moses’ mission, Pharaoh’s support-based turn, casting into the sea, and a sterile wind follow in 51:37–41. **Role and abduction:** the search establishes the household as the sole concrete exception, and surrendered safety explains its coherence; I infer that preservation operates at a relational household scale, not only individual enumeration. **Reading change:** “one house” becomes a compact social container of submission whose survival measures the surrounding collapse.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 51:37–41’s repeated movement from warning to rejected support and destructive medium made the single house look less like a count and more like the last intact relation.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak sözü bir şeyin biçim veya durumunun farklılaşmasını, şeyin başka bir şeyle değiştirilmesini ve bunun alışveriş, yanlış olanı doğru olanla giderme ya da kan bedeline dönme gibi özel gerçekleşmelerini açıkça bir araya getirir. Dal çerçevesi bu iki temel değişim yolunu ve bağımlı örneklerini doğru ayırır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal değişme ve yerine başkasını koyma işlemleriyle sınırlıdır; salt başkalık bildiren dil bilgisel kullanım veya kan bedelinin kendi adı bu dalın çekirdeği değildir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalın değişme ve değiştirme biçimlerini kapsar; yanlış olanı doğruyla giderme, alışverişte karşılıklı değiştirme ve kan bedeline dönme okumalarını yalnız kendi yapılarında tutar.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyin özü aynı kalsa da biçiminin ya da durumunun öncekinden farklı hale getirilmesi veya bir şeyin kaldırılıp yerine başka bir şeyin konmasıdır. Belirli yapılarda yanlış olanı doğru olanla giderme, alışverişte karşılıklı değiştirme ve cana karşılık cezadan kan bedeline dönme biçiminde gerçekleşir.

facets.statement: Bir şeyin biçimini veya durumunu öncekinden farklı hale getirme ve bunun sonucunda şeyin değişmesi temel işlemdir.
Bir şeyi kaldırıp onun yerine başka bir şeyi koyma, değiştirmenin ikinci temel yoludur.
Yanlış veya kabul edilemez olanı, onu giderecek doğru bir uygulamayla değiştirme özel bir gerçekleşmedir.
Alışverişte iki tarafın karşılıkları değiş tokuş etmesi ve bir bedelin ötekinin yerine geçmesi bu çekirdeğe bağlıdır.
Cana karşılık ceza kararının kan bedeline çevrilmesi, yerine koyarak değiştirmenin hukuk bağlamındaki örneğidir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar değişimi iki ana biçimde sunar: aynı şeyin biçim veya durumunun farklılaşması ve bir şeyin yerini başka bir şeyin alması. Yanlış olanı doğruyla giderme, alışverişte değiş tokuş ve cana karşılık cezadan kan bedeline dönme bu iki işlemin bağlama bağlı gerçekleşmeleridir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak sözü aileye, özellikle eşe yönelik kıskanç koruma duygusunu; bu duyguyu taşıyan erkek ve kadın nitelemelerini ve aynı anlamdaki bir söyleyiş çeşidini birlikte verir. Dal çerçevesi duyguyu, taşıyıcısını ve dilsel çeşidini doğru biçimde sınırlar.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal aile veya eşe yönelik kıskanç koruma duygusudur; geçimlik sağlama, kan bedeli, genel değişim ve salt başkalık anlamlarından ayrıdır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım duygu adını, bu duyguyu taşıyan kişiyi bildiren biçimleri ve aile üzerine kurulan eylem yapısını ayırır; aile bağını bütün kullanımlarda korur.

concept_map.definition: Bir kişinin eşini veya ailesini başkasının ilgisinden sakınma, bağlılığını koruma ve bu nedenle kıskançlık duyma eğilimidir; aynı alan bu eğilimi güçlü biçimde taşıyan kişiyi de niteler.

facets.statement: Kişinin eşini veya ailesini başkasının ilgisinden sakınarak bağlılığı korumaya yönelen kıskançlık duygusudur.
Bu duyguyu taşıyan erkek veya kadın, cinsiyete ve yoğunluğa göre çeşitli niteleme biçimleriyle adlandırılır.
Duygu adı için aynı anlamı taşıyan ayrı bir söyleyiş biçimi de aktarılır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar aileye yönelik kıskanç koruma duygusunu, bu duyguya sahip erkek ve kadınların nitelendirilmesini ve duygu adının bir söyleyiş çeşidini birlikte kaydeder. Duygunun hedefi aile bağıdır; genel cesaret veya yalnız sevgi değildir.

Dal çerçevesi bu ad, niteleme ve dil bilgisel işlevleri tek başkalık alanında doğru biçimde toplar.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalın başkalık bildiren biçimleri, dışta bırakma ve olumsuzlama görevlerini ve belirli yapılardaki aykırılık ifadelerini ayrı tutar; yapı görevlerini yalın kökün tek anlamına indirgemez.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyin ötekinden ayrı, başka veya ona aykırı olmasıdır; bu ilişki dil içinde bir unsuru kümenin dışında bırakmak, bir niteliği ya da varlığı olumsuzlamak ve iki şeyin birbirinden farklı olduğunu bildirmek için de kullanılır.

facets.statement: Bir şeyin belirtilen başka bir şeyle aynı olmayıp ondan ayrı, başka veya ona aykırı olması temel ilişkidir.
Bir niteleyici ya da ad olarak kullanıldığında belirli bir varlığı veya biçimi dışlar ve başkasını gösterir.
Bir küme içinden belirtilen unsuru hükmün dışında bırakma görevinde kullanılır.
Bir nitelik, biçim veya varlık için yalın olumsuzluk bildiren görev üstlenir.
İki şeyin birbirinden farklılaşması başkalık ilişkisini karşılıklı olarak kurar; başkalık, yalnız görüş ayrılığından daha geniştir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar başkalığı aynı olmama ve aykırılık ilişkisi olarak verir; bu temel ilişki ad ve niteleyici kullanımına, bir unsuru dışta bırakmaya ve yalın olumsuzlamaya uzanır. Ayrıca karşılıklı farklılaşmayı kapsar ve yalnız anlaşmazlık bildiren daha dar ilişkiyle sınırlı değildir.

identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dalın çekirdeği ısırılmış kişidir; ısırma olayını adlandırma yalnızca tartışmalı bir kaynak değişkesi olarak tutulur.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yalın dal ısırılmış kişi adını taşır; tartışmalı ısırma olayı kullanımı çekirdekle eşitlenmeden kaynak değişkesi olarak belirtilir.

Yılan ısırması olayını adlandırdığı aktarımı başka bir kaynak tarafından kuşkuyla karşılanır.
